authors: Lukas Kühn; Eileen Wengemuth; Lara Kleist; Kyung Eun (Anna) Choi
pain_condition_detail: chronic musculoskeletal pain conditions including chronic low back pain, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, neck pain, rheumatoid arthritis
bps_function_set: background framing; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the biopsychosocial label to frame PNE as addressing biopsychosocial etiology, but the review itself focuses on qualitative determinants of PNE acceptance. Biological content is limited to neurophysiology education topics; psychological content includes kinesiophobia, catastrophizing, anxiety, depression; social content is minimal (clinician-patient relationship, professional culture). No integration across domains is proposed.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper mentions that trust may modulate neural pain processing and that biomedical beliefs may cause skepticism, but no cross-domain pathway or mechanism is specified.
quality_assessment_tools_1: jbi critical appraisal tool for qualitative research
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS language but does not integrate domains, biological content is limited to neurophysiology topics taught in PNE, not as a domain of analysis
conceptual_tensions_2: Social domain is reduced to clinician-patient relationship and professional culture, broader social determinants are absent
conceptual_tensions_3: Psychological constructs (kinesiophobia, catastrophizing, anxiety, depression) are named but never defined or operationalized
additional_observations_1: The review is a qualitative meta-aggregation of determinants of PNE acceptance, not a review of BPS model operationalization. BPS is used as a descriptor for PNE content, not as an analytic framework
additional_observations_2: The paper's main contribution is identifying barriers and facilitators to PNE implementation, not testing or elaborating the BPS model
synthesis_note: This qualitative systematic review uses the biopsychosocial label to frame PNE as addressing biopsychosocial etiology, but the review itself does not operationalize or integrate the three domains. Biological content is limited to neurophysiology topics taught in PNE; psychological constructs are named but undefined; social content is minimal. The paper's contribution is to PNE implementation, not to BPS model testing.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS language is used but social domain is minimal and no integration occurs. Triadic integration is none. Psychological domain dominates as the main analytic thread.

title: Acceptance of pain neuroscience education in chronic musculoskeletal pain conditions: qualitative systematic review
authors: Lukas Kühn; Eileen Wengemuth; Lara Kleist; Kyung Eun (Anna) Choi
pain_condition_detail: Chronic musculoskeletal pain conditions, including chronic low back pain, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, neck pain, gout, and chronic fatigue syndrome.
context_note: Included studies came from England, New Zealand, Australia, the United States, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Lebanon; settings were primary, secondary, or tertiary musculoskeletal care.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; operational definition; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes BPS mainly as the content and scope of PNE: education about pain origins, biopsychosocial etiology, and biological mechanisms. Acceptance is organized around patient beliefs, relevance, setting, clinician relationship, provider confidence, and role clarity. Domains are mostly listed as determinants, not modeled as interacting mechanisms.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper specifies some pathways: trust toward clinicians reduces pain-related neural activity and can support engagement/learning; group settings provide support that may enhance motivation/adherence; PNE biological content is expected to change pain beliefs/behaviours. No triadic mechanism is specified.
quality_assessment_tools_1: jbi critical appraisal tool for qualitative research
emergent_labels_9: professional culture focused on biomedical aspects of care
conceptual_tensions_1: PNE is framed as biopsychosocial, but much of the operational content is biological pain education, so social and psychological domains enter mainly as determinants of acceptance
conceptual_tensions_2: Brain-based pain explanations may reduce tissue-damage beliefs, yet the review reports they can make pain seem invented or psychological
conceptual_tensions_3: Clinicians recognize psychological factors, but the paper finds limited tools, confidence, training, and professional culture barriers to addressing them
conceptual_tensions_4: Group PNE is described as motivating and supportive, but also potentially tiring, hard to remember, and not suitable for all patients
conceptual_tensions_5: The paper calls for mechanistic work on clinician–patient relationship, but explicitly notes a lack of experimental evidence for that relationship
additional_observations_1: The review is not a direct test of BPS as a model, it is a review of determinants of PNE acceptance
additional_observations_2: The BPS label appears in inclusion criteria, but the synthesis organizes findings as facilitators/barriers rather than as domains with specified interactions
additional_observations_3: Included studies were adult chronic musculoskeletal pain patients and healthcare providers from multiple countries and care levels
additional_observations_4: The review excludes pediatric, postsurgical, cancer-related, and pregnancy-related chronic pain
additional_observations_5: PNE variants include video, booklets, metaphors, in-person sessions, group sessions, individualized sessions, and multimodal PNE+
additional_observations_6: The paper relies heavily on qualitative determinants and cites experimental evidence only selectively in the discussion
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly as the content and scope of PNE rather than as a tested explanatory model. Biological and psychological material is central; social factors are mostly implementation determinants. It lists domains and determinants, but does not model a three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: BPS is used as an organizing/operational frame for PNE; all three domains appear, but mainly as parallel determinants of acceptance. Mechanistic pairwise links are noted, especially trust–neural activity, so triadic integration is partial.

title: Acceptance of pain neuroscience education in chronic musculoskeletal pain conditions: qualitative systematic review
authors: Lukas Kühn; Eileen Wengemuth; Lara Kleist; Kyung Eun (Anna) Choi
pain_condition_detail: chronic musculoskeletal pain conditions including low back pain, osteoarthritis, neck pain, fibromyalgia, and others
context_note: International studies from England, New Zealand, Australia, United States, Netherlands, Portugal, and Lebanon
bps_operationalization_summary: PNE is framed as a strategy to manage biopsychosocial aspects of chronic pain, but the review focuses on barriers and facilitators to PNE acceptance rather than operationalizing the BPS model itself. The BPS label is used descriptively to frame PNE's scope.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes that psychological factors (beliefs, relationships, professional culture) influence PNE acceptance and delivery, but does not propose biological or social mechanisms linking to these psychological factors. Integration is primarily directional from psychological to social outcomes.
quality_assessment_tools_1: jbi critical appraisal tool for qualitative research
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between PNE's biopsychosocial framing and its actual focus on biological mechanisms with limited psychological/social integration
conceptual_tensions_2: Tension between patients' biomedical beliefs and PNE's neurocentric explanation of pain
conceptual_tensions_3: Tension between group-based PNE benefits (social support) and individualized delivery needs
additional_observations_1: The review focuses on barriers and facilitators to PNE acceptance rather than operationalizing the BPS model itself
additional_observations_2: Biological content is described in detail but not integrated with psychological or social factors
additional_observations_3: Psychological constructs are well-developed with multiple outcomes documented
additional_observations_4: Social factors are mentioned but not systematically integrated with other domains
additional_observations_5: Religious/spiritual beliefs emerge as contextual factors affecting PNE acceptance
additional_observations_6: Health literacy is identified as a key determinant of PNE effectiveness
synthesis_note: This review examines barriers and facilitators to pain neuroscience education acceptance in chronic musculoskeletal pain. While PNE is framed as a biopsychosocial intervention, the review primarily focuses on psychological factors (beliefs, relationships) and mentions biological mechanisms without substantive integration. Social factors are limited to clinician-patient relationships. The BPS label is used descriptively rather than as an integrated analytical framework.
coding_rationale: BPS typology is 'multifactorial' because all three domains are present but not integrated. Psychological domain is 'elaborated' with multiple constructs and outcomes. Biological and social domains are 'mentioned' but lack integration. No triadic integration proposed.
